# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement is not credited for being cheap.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.
2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.
3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.
Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.
4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.
Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.
5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN

--- page 2
The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.
Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.
6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.
The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.
7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.

===== 30_seismic/DAP-2_Diaphragm_Analysis_Protocol_REV1.pdf 3
--- page 1
Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT
DAP-2
REVISION
1
DATE
2026-07-31
TITLE
DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL
ISSUED BY
Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
1. PURPOSE
This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a
design whose own analysis differs from it will be assessed on the protocol's results.
2. THE TWO STAGES
Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.
3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation θ. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are
both included:
    fuu = h³/(3EI) + h/(GAv),   fuθ = h²/(2EI),   fθθ = h/EI,    kvv = EA/h
with Ec = 57,000√f'c psi for f'c = 6000 psi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area, and I taken as 0.50 Ig (cracked, ACI
318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)). The axial stiffness uses the gross area. A segment interrupted over part of its height by an
opening that does not reach the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are
factored by the solid fraction of the height.
Adjacent panels are connected by the vertical shear spring formed by their joint connectors: the spring stiffness is the
number of connectors in the joint times the connector stiffness of the manufacturer's table, and it acts on the relative
vertical slip of the two panel edges,
    slip = (vi + θi Li/2) − (vi+1 − θi+1 Li+1/2).
The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement. Condensing the
segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness kseg; recovering the internal state for a unit segment
force gives the shear in every joint and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force. A panel's tie-down
carries its own base couple, taken on an internal lever arm of 0.8 times the panel length, plus the coupling axial force
delivered to it.
4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
    D = diag(A′, A′, G′)
where G′ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A′ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.

--- page 2
Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor Ax is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
    flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.
    rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.
    semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.
6.4 Orthogonal cases. For the cases the design criteria mark 100/30, the demands are those of the case direction
plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign
of accidental eccentricity and same stage.

--- page 3

Case. A single wall segment 40.0 ft long, on a wall line with no openings within the segment, built from four 10.0 ft

c=np.load('/tmp/centers.npy')
# mapping cluster order 4->CP1, 1->CP2, 2->CP3, 3->CP4
src=np.array([c[3],c[0],c[1],c[2]])
dst=np.array([[6.5,4.25,5.4],[233.75,5.1,5.55],[234.6,174.2,5.35],[7.2,175.4,5.6]])
def umeyama(src,dst,scale=True):
    mu_s=src.mean(0); mu_d=dst.mean(0)
    S=src-mu_s; D=dst-mu_d
    C=D.T@S/len(src)
    U,s,Vt=np.linalg.svd(C)
    d=np.sign(np.linalg.det(U@Vt))
    Dm=np.diag([1,1,d])
    R=U@Dm@Vt
    var=(S**2).sum()/len(src)
    k=(s*np.diag(Dm)).sum()/var if scale else 1.0
    t=mu_d-k*R@mu_s
    return k,R,t
for sc in (False,True):
    k,R,t=umeyama(src,dst,sc)
    pred=(k*(R@src.T)).T+t
    print('scale',sc,k); print(R); print(t); print('resid',pred-dst)
    print('rot angle deg about z', np.degrees(np.arctan2(R[1,0],R[0,0])))
# 2D fit
"

DESIGNATED SEISMIC SYSTEMS [Replacement] 
The designated seismic system of a structure consists of those nonstructural 
components that require design in accordance with Chapter 13 and for which the 
component importance factor, Ip, is greater than 1.0. This designation applies to 
systems that are required to be operational following the design earthquake.

Moment Frame [Replacement]  
A frame in which members and joints resist lateral forces by flexure as well as 
along the axis of the members.  Moment frames are categorized as intermediate 
moment frames (IMF), ordinary moment frames (OMF), and special moment 
frames (SMF).  Every joint must be restrained against rotation.

2020 NEHRP Provisions Design Examples 
FEMA P-2192-V1

Chapter 7: Horizontal Diaphragm 
Design 
Kelly Cobeen1  
7.1 Overview  
The 2020 Edition of the NEHRP Recommended Seismic Provisions for New Buildings and Other 
Structures (FEMA, 2020), referred to herein as the Provisions, includes three significant items 
related to the design of diaphragms that represent changes between the 2015 Provisions (FEMA, 
2016), and 2020 Provisions. These have resulted in matching changes between ASCE/SEI 7-16 
(ASCE, 2017) and ASCE/SEI 7-22 (ASCE, 2021). First, ASCE/SEI 7-16 Section 12.10.3 (Alternative 
Design Provisions for Diaphragms including Chords and Collectors) was expanded to permit use of 
bare steel deck diaphragms. Second, new Section 12.10.4 has been added, containing alternative 
diaphragm seismic design provisions for one-story structures with flexible diaphragms and rigid 
vertical elements (commonly designated as rigid-wall flexible-diaphragm (RWFD) buildings). Third, the 
ASCE/SEI 7-16 Section 12.10.3 alternative design provisions have been further expanded to permit 
use of concrete filled steel deck diaphragms. This is based in part on Resource Paper 6 in Part 3 of 
the 2020 NEHRP Provisions (FEMA P-1082-2).  
This chapter addresses use of the ASCE/SEI 7-22 diaphragm design provisions, including these 
three significant changes. The primary focus of this chapter is the determination of diaphragm 
seismic design forces. The horizontal distribution of these forces and design for shear and flexure 
are not addressed as this can vary depending on the classification of the diaphragm (flexible, semi-
rigid or rigid), the approach taken to analytical modeling of the structure, and the diaphragm system. 
In accordance with Section 12.3.4.1, rho () is assumed to be 1.0 for diaphragm design and 
therefore not included in this discussion. Similarly, effects that might be triggered by plan 
irregularities are not discussed. While these effects are ignored for the purposes of these example 
problems, such effects are required to be appropriately considered in design of structures. Further 
information on seismic design of diaphragms can be found in the NEHRP Seismic Design Technical 
Brief Series, as included in the other resources section that follows; while these briefs do not 
address the ASCE/SEI 7-22 revisions, they provide a wealth of information on other aspects of 
diaphragm design. 
1 Kelly Cobeen, S.E., Wiss, Janney, Elstner Associates, Inc. 
=========== page 2
2020 NEHRP Provisions Design Examples 
248 
FEMA P-2192-V1 
Other Changes Between ASCE/SEI 7-16 and 7-22 
A number of other changes between ASCE/SEI 7-16 and 7-22 could potentially affect the 
design of diaphragms. Two in particular are worth mentioning in conjunction with diaphragm 
design: 
▪ 
First, significant changes have occurred to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.4, Seismic Ground 
Motion Values, including the inclusion of a multi-period response spectrum in Section 
11.4.5. For purposes of diaphragm design, it is intended, however, that the design spectral 
acceleration parameters of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.4.4 be used where SDS and SD1 
values are needed; for this reason, the change to Section 11.4.5 is not intended to affect 
diaphragm design.  
▪ 
Second, significant changes have been made to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.8.6 and 
12.12, addressing deflection and drift. These changes do potentially affect diaphragm 
design and are discussed in this chapter. 
For further discussion of diaphragm deflections, the reader is referred to Section 7.2, FEMA P-
1026 (FEMA, 2021), Resource Paper 8 from FEMA P-2082-2, and the previously mentioned 
NEHRP Tech Brief series. 
The following are included in this chapter: 
▪ 
Section 7.2 introduces the three diaphragm seismic design methods included in ASCE/SEI 7-22. 
▪ 
Section 7.3 provides step-by-step descriptions of the implementation of the three available 
diaphragm design methods. 
▪ 
Section 7.4 provides example calculations for a one-story wood assembly hall, using the 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 traditional design method and repeated using the 
Section 12.10.3 alternative design provisions. 
▪ 
Section 7.5 provides example calculations for a multi-story steel building with concrete filled 
metal deck floor diaphragms and a bare steel deck roof diaphragm using the ASCE/SEI 7-22 
Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 traditional design method and repeated using the Section 12.10.3 
alternative design provisions. 
▪ 
Finally, Section 7.6 provides example calculations for a one-story concrete tilt-up building with a

7.2 Introduction to Diaphragm Seismic Design Methods 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10, Diaphragms, Chords and Collectors, includes three separate methods 
for seismic design of diaphragms and their chords and collectors. Included is the traditional 
diaphragm design method in accordance with the provisions of Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2, the 
alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3, and the new alternative RWFD provisions of Section 
12.10.4. For a given diaphragm, one of these three methods will need to be selected by the designer 
and implemented. Where a group of diaphragms is similar enough in elevation that they would be 
anticipated to interact, the use of one diaphragm design method for the group of diaphragms is 
recommended. 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 traditional provisions were the only diaphragm design 
method available until the Section 12.10.3 provisions were added in the 2015 NEHRP Provisions 
and ASCE/SEI 7-16. When using Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2, diaphragm design forces are 
determined based on the seismic design parameters of the vertical elements of the seismic force-
resisting system without consideration of the effect of the diaphragm system on the response of the 
structure. Use of this method is permitted for all structures, with the exception of precast concrete 
diaphragms in Seismic Design Categories (SDC) C through F. 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.3 provides alternative diaphragm seismic design provisions that 
explicitly recognize and account for the effect of diaphragm ductility and displacement capacity on 
the diaphragm design forces. This is accomplished with the introduction of a diaphragm design force

251 
reduction factor, Rs. Neither the number of stories nor the building configuration is restricted by the 
Section 12.10.3 provisions; however, diaphragm construction is limited to the diaphragm systems 
specifically noted within those provisions. 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.3 is mandatory for precast concrete diaphragms in structures 
assigned to SDC C, D, E and F. It is optional for all other diaphragm types and SDCs for which the 
alternative design method is applicable. The mandate for use of Section 12.10.3 for precast 
diaphragm systems in SDC C through F is based on recent research (Fleischman et al., 2012) that 
indicates that improved earthquake performance can be attained through recognition of the ductility 
and deformation capacity based on diaphragm detailing used. Without use of the Section 12.10.3 
provisions for precast diaphragms, the seismic performance might be less than that targeted by the 
NEHRP Provisions and ASCE/SEI 7. At the same time, many conventional diaphragm systems 
designed in accordance with ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 have performed 
adequately; continued use of Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 is therefore considered reasonable for 
diaphragm systems other than those for which Section 12.10.3 is mandated.  
Design of Cast-in-Place Concrete Equivalent Precast Diaphragms 
It is worth noting that ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 14.2.2.1 defines a category of precast concrete 
diaphragms designated as “cast-in-place concrete equivalent precast diaphragms.” This 
diaphragm type uses either a noncomposite cast-in-place diaphragm over precast sections or a 
precast diaphragm with cast-in-place closure strips. For this type of diaphragm, use of 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.3 is not mandated, allowing the traditional design method of 
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 to be used. 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.4 introduces diaphragm seismic design provisions that are permitted 
to be used for one-story structures combining flexible diaphragms with rigid vertical elements. This 
alternative RWFD seismic design methodology specifically recognizes the seismic response of these 
structures as being dominated by dynamic response of and inelastic behavior in the diaphragm. 
While the most common occurrences of this structure type are the concrete tilt-up and masonry “big-
box” buildings, the rigid vertical element terminology of this section recognizes a wider range of 
vertical elements for which this methodology is permitted to be used. The primary use of Section 
12.10.4 provisions is intended to be for structures where one or more spans of the diaphragm 
exceeds 100 feet; however, use for structures in which diaphragm spans are less than 100 feet is 
not precluded. Table 7-1 provides an overview of the three available diaphragm design methods. 
Changes have been made to the displacement and drift provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.8.6 
and 12.12 that potentially affect the design of diaphragms. Per ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.8.6.3 and 
12.8.6.4, the design earthquake displacement and maximum considered earthquake displacement 
are to be calculated, including the diaphragm defection. When computing the design story drift, 
however, the diaphragm deflection is permitted to be neglected; as a result, the ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 
12.12.1 check against the allowable story drift does not need to consider diaphragm deflection. For 
further discussion of diaphragm deflections, the reader is referred to FEMA P-1026 (FEMA, 2021),

7.3 Step-By-Step Determination of Diaphragm Design 
Forces  
The step-by-step descriptions in Section 7.3 are intended to provide a high-level overview of 
implementation of the three diaphragm design methods. See the examples that follow and ASCE/SEI 
7-22 and commentary for more detail. The step-by-step descriptions focus on use of the ASCE/SEI 7-
22 equivalent lateral force (ELF) procedure; some modifications are needed when using linear 
dynamic analysis procedures. This step-by-step description also focuses primarily on diaphragm 
inertial forces due to the mass tributary to each diaphragm level. Where diaphragm transfer forces 
as defined in ASCE/SEI Section 11.2 occur, they are required to be addressed in accordance with 
ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10.1.1 or 12.10.3.3, as applicable.  
In order to perform seismic analysis of the SFRS and diaphragms, it is necessary to define the 
diaphragm flexibility in accordance with ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3. This section sets criteria by 
which diaphragms can be idealized as flexible, idealized as rigid, or calculated as flexible. Where 
these do not apply, the diaphragm is required to be modeled as semi-rigid. Where diaphragms are 
designated as rigid or semi-rigid for modeling and design, the process of seismic design will start 
with overall modeling of the building and then proceed to diaphragm design. Regardless of 
diaphragm designation, the seismic design of the diaphragm and vertical elements usually proceed 
in parallel. 
7.3.1 Step-By-Step Determination of Diaphragm Design Forces Using the 
Section 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 Traditional Method 
The following describes in a step-by-step fashion the determination of diaphragm seismic design 
forces using ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The procedure in these sections has 
been in use since before the first edition of the IBC and has, in the past, been applicable to 
diaphragms of all materials. ASCE/SEI 7-22 Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 can no longer be used for 
design of precast concrete diaphragms in structures assigned to SDC C through F, as noted in 
Exception 1 to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.10. 
Step 1: Determine wi, W and wpx. ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.7.2 defines effective seismic weight, W. 
wi is the portion of W that is tributary to level i (Figure 7-1). wpx is different from wi only in that the 
weights of the walls parallel to the earthquake forces are permitted to be excluded from wpx. It is 
common practice to exclude the weights of these parallel walls in low-rise buildings with concrete or 
masonry walls; including or excluding this weight (i.e., using a value of wpx less than wi) is at the 
discretion of the design engineer.

import numpy as np
A=np.load('/tmp/scan_bldg.npy')
x,y,z,I=A.T
cfg={'S':(np.abs(y-0)<0.7, x, y-0, 240),'N':(np.abs(y-180)<0.7, x, 180-y, 240),'W':(np.abs(x-0)<0.7, y, x-0, 180),'E':(np.abs(x-240)<0.7, y, 240-x, 180)}
res={}
for w,(m,s,d,L) in cfg.items():
    s=s[m]; d=d[m]; zz=z[m]
    b=np.arange(-0.5,L+0.5,0.05)
    idx=np.digitize(s,b)-1
    tot=np.bincount(idx,minlength=len(b))
    deep=np.bincount(idx[d>0.045],minlength=len(b))
    frac=np.where(tot>0,deep/np.maximum(tot,1),0)
    cand=np.where(frac>0.3)[0]
    # group
    groups=[]
    for k in cand:
        if groups and k-groups[-1][-1]<=2: groups[-1].append(k)
        else: groups.append([k])
    out=[]
    for g in groups:
        c=(b[g[0]]+b[g[-1]]+0.05)/2
        out.append(round(c,2))
    res[w]=out
    print(w,len(out),out)

    ss=s[sel]; dd=d[sel]; zz=z[sel]; ii=I[sel]

    u=np.unique(np.round(ss,2))

    print(' deepest', [(round(ss[k],2),round(dd[k],3),round(zz[k],1)) for k in o])
    # intensity anomalies
    o=np.argsort(ii)[:5]
    print(' low I', [(round(ss[k],2),round(ii[k],1),round(zz[k],1)) for k in o])

import numpy as np
FC=6000.0
EC=57000*np.sqrt(FC)/1000.0   # ksi
GC=EC/2.4
T_IN=8.0
H_IN=28*12.0

def panel_flex(L_ft, factor=1.0, h_in=H_IN):
    L=L_ft*12.0
    Ig=T_IN*L**3/12.0
    EI=EC*0.5*Ig*factor
    GAv=GC*(5.0/6.0)*T_IN*L*factor
    EA=EC*T_IN*L   # gross area (axial) - not factored? keep gross
    fuu=h_in**3/(3*EI)+h_in/GAv
    fut=h_in**2/(2*EI)
    ftt=h_in/EI
    kvv=EA/h_in
    return fuu,fut,ftt,kvv

def segment(panels, nconn=0, kconn=0.0, factor=1.0, sign=+1, factor_axial=False):
    """panels: list of widths (ft). returns dict with kseg and per-unit-force results.
    DOFs: global u (common), then per panel v_i, th_i."""
    n=len(panels)
    ndof=1+2*n
    K=np.zeros((ndof,ndof))
    for i,L in enumerate(panels):
        fuu,fut,ftt,kvv=panel_flex(L,factor)
        if factor_axial:
            kvv*=factor
        F=np.array([[fuu,sign*fut],[sign*fut,ftt]])
        Kp=np.linalg.inv(F)
        idx=[0,1+2*i+1]  # u, theta
        for a in range(2):
            for b in range(2):
                K[idx[a],idx[b]]+=Kp[a,b]
        K[1+2*i,1+2*i]+=kvv
    kj=nconn*kconn
    if kj>0:
        for i in range(n-1):
            Li=panels[i]*12.0; Lj=panels[i+1]*12.0
            # slip = (v_i + th_i Li/2) - (v_j - th_j Lj/2)
            B=np.zeros(ndof)
            B[1+2*i]=1; B[1+2*i+1]=Li/2
            B[1+2*(i+1)]=-1; B[1+2*(i+1)+1]=Lj/2
            K+=kj*np.outer(B,B)
    # condense on u
    Kuu=K[0,0]; Kur=K[0,1:]; Krr=K[1:,1:]
    kseg=Kuu-Kur@np.linalg.solve(Krr,Kur)
    # unit force: u = 1/kseg
    u=1.0/kseg
    r=-np.linalg.solve(Krr,Kur*u)
    d=np.r_[u,r]
    res={'kseg':kseg,'panels':list(panels)}
    joints=[]
    for i in range(n-1):
        Li=panels[i]*12.0; Lj=panels[i+1]*12.0
        slip=(d[1+2*i]+d[1+2*i+1]*Li/2)-(d[1+2*(i+1)]-d[1+2*(i+1)+1]*Lj/2)
        joints.append(kj*slip)
    res['joint_shear']=joints
    pan=[]
    for i,L in enumerate(panels):
        fuu,fut,ftt,kvv=panel_flex(L,factor)
        if factor_axial: kvv*=factor
        F=np.array([[fuu,sign*fut],[sign*fut,ftt]])
        Kp=np.linalg.inv(F)
        uu=d[0]; th=d[1+2*i+1]; v=d[1+2*i]
        P,M=Kp@np.array([uu,th])   # top shear and top moment (end forces at the free end)
        N=kvv*v
        # base moment = P*h + M_top (statics of cantilever: base moment = P*h - (-M)?)
        Mb_a=P*H_IN+M
        Mb_b=P*H_IN-M
        pan.append({'L':L,'P':P,'Mtop':M,'N':N,'Mb_a':Mb_a,'Mb_b':Mb_b})
    res['panel']=pan
    return res

if __name__=='__main__':
    r=segment([10,10,10,10],3,320.0)
    print('kseg',r['kseg'])
    print('joints',r['joint_shear'])
    for p in r['panel']: print(p)
    r0=segment([10,10,10,10],0,0)
    print('kseg isolated',r0['kseg'])
    r=segment([10,10,10,10],3,320.0,sign=-1)
    print('sign -1: kseg',r['kseg'],'joints',r['joint_shear'])
    for p in r['panel']: print(p)

import numpy as np, scipy.sparse as sp, scipy.sparse.linalg as spla
from geom import *
from stagea import segment as stageA

A_PRIME = 1740.0   # kip/in
E_STEEL = 29000.0
DX = 10.0          # ft
NX, NY = int(LX/DX), int(LY/DX)

def snap(v): return round(v/DX)*DX

class Mesh:
    def __init__(self, xmax=LX):
        self.xmax=xmax
        nx=int(round(xmax/DX)); ny=NY
        self.nx, self.ny = nx, ny
        # elements
        els=[]
        for j in range(ny):
            for i in range(nx):
                xc=(i+0.5)*DX; yc=(j+0.5)*DX
                inside=False
                for _,x0,y0,x1,y1 in ROOF_OPENINGS:
                    if x0<xc<x1 and y0<yc<y1: inside=True
                if inside: continue
                zone=None
                for z,(a,b,c,d) in ZONES.items():
                    if a<=xc<c and b<=yc<d: zone=z
                els.append((i,j,zone))
        self.els=els
        used=set()
        for i,j,z in els:
            for (a,b) in [(i,j),(i+1,j),(i+1,j+1),(i,j+1)]: used.add((a,b))
        self.nodes=sorted(used,key=lambda t:(t[1],t[0]))
        self.nid={n:k for k,n in enumerate(self.nodes)}
        self.nn=len(self.nodes)
        self.xy=np.array([(a*DX,b*DX) for a,b in self.nodes])
        # Q4 base stiffness components (unit D entries) for square element side a (in)
        a=DX*12.0
        g=1/np.sqrt(3)
        self.Kparts={}
        KA=np.zeros((8,8)); KG=np.zeros((8,8))
        self.Bc=None
        for xi in (-g,g):
            for eta in (-g,g):
                B=self._B(xi,eta,a)
                detJ=(a/2)**2
                DA=np.diag([1,1,0.0]); DG=np.diag([0,0,1.0])
                KA+=B.T@DA@B*detJ
                KG+=B.T@DG@B*detJ
        self.KA=KA; self.KG=KG
        self.Bc=self._B(0,0,a)
    @staticmethod
    def _B(xi,eta,a):
        # nodes ordered (-1,-1),(1,-1),(1,1),(-1,1)
        dN_dxi=np.array([-(1-eta),(1-eta),(1+eta),-(1+eta)])/4
        dN_deta=np.array([-(1-xi),-(1+xi),(1+xi),(1-xi)])/4
        dN_dx=dN_dxi*2/a; dN_dy=dN_deta*2/a
        B=np.zeros((3,8))
        B[0,0::2]=dN_dx; B[1,1::2]=dN_dy
        B[2,0::2]=dN_dy; B[2,1::2]=dN_dx
        return B
    def edofs(self,i,j):
        ns=[(i,j),(i+1,j),(i+1,j+1),(i,j+1)]
        d=[]
        for n in ns:
            k=self.nid[n]; d+= [2*k,2*k+1]
        return d

def wall_segments_springs(mesh, wall, kseg_by_seg, segs):
    """returns list of (node_index, dof(0=x,1=y), k, segid)"""
    out=[]
    for s in segs:
        a=s['start']; b=a+s['length']; k=kseg_by_seg[s['id']]
        L=s['length']
        if wall in 'SN':
            yy = 0.0 if wall=='S' else LY
            for xn in np.arange(0,mesh.xmax+1e-9,DX):
                ov=max(0.0,min(b,xn+DX/2)-max(a,xn-DX/2))
                if ov<=1e-9: continue
                key=(int(round(xn/DX)),int(round(yy/DX)))
                if key not in mesh.nid: continue
                out.append((mesh.nid[key],0,k*ov/L,s['id']))
        else:
            xx = 0.0 if wall=='W' else LX
            if xx>mesh.xmax+1e-9: continue
            for yn in np.arange(0,LY+1e-9,DX):
                ov=max(0.0,min(b,yn+DX/2)-max(a,yn-DX/2))
                if ov<=1e-9: continue
                key=(int(round(xx/DX)),int(round(yn/DX)))
                if key not in mesh.nid: continue
                out.append((mesh.nid[key],1,k*ov/L,s['id']))
    return out

def line_bars(mesh, lines_members):
    """returns dict mesh-edge -> list of (line, EA)"""
    bars={}
    for ln,mem in lines_members.items():
        if mem in (None,'C0'): continue
        d,at,f,t,kind=LINES[ln]
        A=MEMBERS[mem][1]; EA=E_STEEL*A
        at_s=snap(at); f_s=snap(f); t_s=snap(t)
        if d=='X':
            j=int(round(at_s/DX))
            for i in range(int(round(f_s/DX)),int(round(t_s/DX))):
                n1=(i,j); n2=(i+1,j)
                if n1 in mesh.nid and n2 in mesh.nid:
                    bars.setdefault((n1,n2),[]).append((ln,EA))
        else:
            i=int(round(at_s/DX))
            for j in range(int(round(f_s/DX)),int(round(t_s/DX))):
                n1=(i,j); n2=(i,j+1)
                if n1 in mesh.nid and n2 in mesh.nid:
                    bars.setdefault((n1,n2),[]).append((ln,EA))
    return bars

def assemble(mesh, deck, bars, springs, rigid=False):
    nd=2*mesh.nn
    rows=[];cols=[];vals=[]
    mult=1e7 if rigid else 1.0
    for (i,j,z) in mesh.els:
        Gp=DECK[deck[z]][1]
        Ke=(A_PRIME*mesh.KA+Gp*mesh.KG)*mult
        d=mesh.edofs(i,j)
        for a in range(8):
            for b in range(8):
                rows.append(d[a]);cols.append(d[b]);vals.append(Ke[a,b])
    for (n1,n2),lst in bars.items():
        EA=sum(e for _,e in lst)
        L=DX*12.0
        k=EA/L
        k1=mesh.nid[n1];k2=mesh.nid[n2]
        dof=0 if n1[1]==n2[1] else 1
        d1=2*k1+dof; d2=2*k2+dof
        for a,b,v in [(d1,d1,k),(d2,d2,k),(d1,d2,-k),(d2,d1,-k)]:
            rows.append(a);cols.append(b);vals.append(v)
    for (n,dof,k,sid) in springs:
        rows.append(2*n+dof);cols.append(2*n+dof);vals.append(k)
    K=sp.csr_matrix((vals,(rows,cols)),shape=(nd,nd))
    return K

def node_masses(mesh, direction, mass_case, stage):
    """mass (kips weight) per node applied to diaphragm, for loading direction 'X' or 'Y'."""
    m=np.zeros(mesh.nn)
    a=DX*DX*ROOF_PSF/1000.0
    for (i,j,z) in mesh.els:
        for n in [(i,j),(i+1,j),(i+1,j+1),(i,j+1)]:
            m[mesh.nid[n]]+=a/4
    # RTUs
    for tag,x,y,wlb,ph in RTUS:
        if ph==2 and mass_case!='future': continue
        if x>mesh.xmax+1e-9: continue

        for yy in (0.0,LY):

                    else: trib=DX
                    if mesh.xmax<LX and abs(px-mesh.xmax)<1e-6: trib=DX/2

    """shear flow (plf) at element centroid; returns dict (i,j)->(q, zone)"""
    out={}
    mult=1e7 if rigid else 1.0
    for (i,j,z) in mesh.els:
        d=mesh.edofs(i,j)
        eps=mesh.Bc@u[d]
        q=DECK[deck[z]][1]*mult*eps[2]   # kip/in
        out[(i,j)]=(q*12000.0,z)
    return out

def zone_shears(mesh, sf):
    """DAP-2 6.1: largest section mean over mesh lines crossing each zone."""
    res={}
    for z,(x0,y0,x1,y1) in ZONES.items():
        best=0.0
        i0,i1=int(x0/DX),int(x1/DX); j0,j1=int(y0/DX),int(y1/DX)
        if i0>=mesh.nx: res[z]=0.0; continue
        i1=min(i1,mesh.nx)
        for j in range(j0,j1):
            v=[abs(sf[(i,j)][0]) for i in range(i0,i1) if (i,j) in sf]
            if v: best=max(best,np.mean(v))
        for i in range(i0,i1):
            v=[abs(sf[(i,j)][0]) for j in range(j0,j1) if (i,j) in sf]
            if v: best=max(best,np.mean(v))
        res[z]=best
    return res

def flexible_case(model, direction, mass_case, stage):

    seg={}; coll={}

    return res

import numpy as np, time, json, sys
from evaluate import *
PAT=['P1','P2','P3','P4','P5']
def evaluate_deck(deck, base, cases, shear_margin=0.95, defl_margin=0.97):
    d=dict(base); d['deck']=dict(deck)
    E,env,rep=check(d,cases)
    U=utilizations(d,env,E)
    viol={}
    for z in ZONES:
        u=U[('zone',z)]/shear_margin
        if u>1: viol[('zone',z)]=u
    u=U[('defl_all',)]/defl_margin
    if u>1: viol[('defl',)]=u
    return U,viol,env,rep
def deck_cost(deck):
    c,_,_,_=cost({'deck':deck,'lines':{},'walls':{w:{'jc':'JC0','n':0,'ba':'BA1','wa':'WA1','wa_s':10} for w in 'SNWE'},'sfrs':'intermediate_precast'})
    return c['deck']
def optimize(base, cases, start=None, shear_margin=0.95, defl_margin=0.97, verbose=True):
    deck=dict(start) if start else {z:'P1' for z in ZONES}

        if verbose: print(it,'cost',deck_cost(deck),{z:deck[z] for z in ZONES},'viol',{k:round(v,3) for k,v in viol.items()}); sys.stdout.flush()
        if not viol: break
        # shear violations first: bump each violating zone to the minimum adequate pattern
        moved=False
        for k,v in viol.items():
            if k[0]=='zone':
                z=k[1]; dem=env[('zone',z)][0]
                for p in PAT:
                    if 0.6*DECK[p][0]*shear_margin>=dem:
                        break
                if PAT.index(p)>PAT.index(deck[z]):
                    deck[z]=p; moved=True
                elif PAT.index(deck[z])<4:
                    deck[z]=PAT[PAT.index(deck[z])+1]; moved=True
        if moved: continue
        # deflection: try one-step upgrades, choose best reduction per $
        u0=U[('defl_all',)]
        best=None
        for z in ZONES:
            i=PAT.index(deck[z])
            if i==4: continue
            t=dict(deck); t[z]=PAT[i+1]
            Ut,_,_,_=evaluate_deck(t,base,cases,shear_margin,defl_margin)
            dc=deck_cost(t)-deck_cost(deck)
            gain=(u0-Ut[('defl_all',)])/dc
            if best is None or gain>best[0]: best=(gain,z)
        deck[best[1]]=PAT[PAT.index(deck[best[1]])+1]
    # downgrade pass
    improved=True
    while improved:
        improved=False
        for z in sorted(ZONES,key=lambda z:-deck_cost({**deck})):
            i=PAT.index(deck[z])
            if i==0: continue
            t=dict(deck); t[z]=PAT[i-1]
            Ut,vt,_,_=evaluate_deck(t,base,cases,shear_margin,defl_margin)
            if not vt:
                deck=t; improved=True
                if verbose: print('downgrade',z,'->',t[z],'cost',deck_cost(deck))
    return deck
if __name__=='__main__':
    base={'sfrs':'intermediate_precast','lines':{ln:'C1' for ln in LINES},
          'walls':{w:{'jc':'JC0','n':0,'ba':'BA2','wa':'WA2','wa_s':10} for w in 'SNWE'}}
    mode=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else 'all'
    cases=all_cases()
    if mode=='shown': cases=[c for c in cases if c[0].startswith('S')]
    if mode=='final': cases=[c for c in cases if c[5]=='final']
    t=time.time()
    deck=optimize(base,cases)
    print('FINAL',mode,deck,deck_cost(deck),'time',time.time()-t)

 'brace_cap':12.0,'brace_s':20.0,
}
STEEL_ANCHOR_FACTOR=1.4

def anchorage():
    ka={}
    out={}
    for w in 'SNWE':
        Lf = LX if w in 'SN' else LY      # span of diaphragm parallel to the anchored wall (UFC Fig 3-1)
        k=min(2.0,1.0+Lf/100.0)
        Wp=WALL_PLF*1000.0                # plf, includes parapet lever action
        Fp=max(0.4*SDS*k*IE*Wp, 0.2*k*IE*Wp)
        out[w]=dict(Lf=Lf,ka=k,Wp=Wp,Fp=Fp,Fp_eq1=0.4*SDS*k*IE*Wp,Fp_min=0.2*k*IE*Wp)
    return out

def run(design=DESIGN, cases=None):
    E,env,rep=check(design,cases)
    U=utilizations(design,env,E)
    anc=anchorage()
    for w in 'SNWE':
        wd=design['walls'][w]
        cap=PHI_WA*WA[wd['wa']][0]
        dem=anc[w]['Fp']/1000.0*wd['wa_s']
        U[('anchor',w)]=dem*STEEL_ANCHOR_FACTOR/cap
        U[('subdiaphragm',w)]=(wd['sub_s']/wd['sub_d'])/2.5
        # subdiaphragm shear vs weakest adjacent zone
        zs={'S':['Z1','Z2','Z3','Z4'],'N':['Z9','Z10','Z11','Z12'],'W':['Z1','Z5','Z9'],'E':['Z4','Z8','Z12']}[w]
        vsub=anc[w]['Fp']*wd['sub_s']/(2*wd['sub_d'])
        U[('subshear',w)]=vsub/min(PHI_DECK*DECK[design['deck'][z]][0] for z in zs)
    # erection bracing: 0.5 x Fp on braced wall, tributary spacing
    Fpb=0.5*max(a['Fp'] for a in anc.values())/1000.0*design['brace_s']
    U[('brace',)]=Fpb/design['brace_cap']
    return E,env,rep,U,anc

if __name__=='__main__':
    E,env,rep,U,anc=run()
    for k in sorted(U,key=lambda k:-U[k])[:25]: print(k,round(U[k],3))
    print(cost(DESIGN)[0])
    print(anc)

results.content:
# Building B - seismic diaphragm and shear wall design basis

Design format: LRFD

All loads in this package are strength-level seismic load effects (1.0E, rho = 1.0 where noted) and all capacities are LRFD design strengths (phi x nominal) of the referenced standard. No ASD values are used anywhere (SDC-02 s.9). Units are ft, kips, plf.

## 1. Seismic basis

* Code: 2024 IBC as adopted by Montana (ARM 24.301.131); ASCE/SEI 7-22; ACI 318-19; AISI S310 (SDC-02 s.1).
* Risk Category III, Ie = 1.25 - Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant (OBD-CDDC-B s.1.4, SDC-02 s.2, ASCE 7-22 s.11.5.1 / Table 1.5-2). The Risk Category II block on the architectural cover sheet is superseded by SDC-02.
* Site Class D from the measured Vs,100 = 905 ft/s of boring B-204 (GEO-2026-071 s.4, SDC-02 s.3).
* SDS = 0.44 g, SD1 = 0.24 g from the USGS ASCE7-22 web-service output for Risk Category III, Site Class D, 46.6832 / -111.9756 (project/30_seismic). Ts = 0.545 s.
* SDC from SDS = C, from SD1 = D; the more severe governs -> **SDC D** (ASCE 7-22 s.11.6, SDC-02 s.3). The 12.10-type 11.6 exception is not available because the diaphragm is flexible with spans > 40 ft.
* Ta = Ct hn^x = 0.02 x 28^0.75 = 0.243 s (Eq. 12.8-7). Cs = SDS/(R/Ie) = 0.44/(4/1.25) = 0.1375 (Eq. 12.8-2); Eq. 12.8-3 limit 0.308 does not govern; Eq. 12.8-5 minimum 0.0242.
* Effective seismic weight W = roof 20 psf x 39200 sf net = 784.0 k + phase 1 RTUs 45.0 k + walls 1441.5 k = **2270.5 kips** (future mass case 2286.5 k). Base shear **V = 312.2 kips** (future 314.4 k). Single storey: Fx = V at the roof.
* Wall weight tributary to the roof uses the lever action of the 3 ft parapet cantilever (SDC-02 s.6, FEMA P-2192-V1 s.7.6.1 Step 1): w = 100 psf x 31 ft x (31/2) ft / 28 ft = 1716.1 plf, i.e. a tributary height of 17.16 ft (not 28/2 + 3 = 17.0 ft).
* Diaphragm force (ASCE 7-22 s.12.10.1.1): Fpx/wpx = sum Fi / sum wi = Cs = 0.1375, between 0.2 SDS Ie = 0.110 and 0.4 SDS Ie = 0.220. wpx(X) = 1446.8 k -> Fpx = 198.9 k, w_px = 1105 plf over the 180 ft span; wpx(Y) = 1652.7 k -> Fpx = 227.2 k, w_px = 947 plf over the 240 ft span. The wall lines parallel to the loading carry their own inertia directly (DAP-2 s.5).
* Construction stage (S11, S12): 0.5 x the permanent seismic load, Ie, R and accidental torsion unchanged (ERC-07 s.3, ASCE/SEI 37-14), deck fastened west of X = 180 ft only (ERC-07 s.4).
* Redundancy: rho = 1.0 for the diaphragm, collectors (Omega0 effects) and wall anchorage (ASCE 7-22 s.12.3.4.1); for the walls rho = 1.0 per s.12.3.4.2(b) (regular plan, at least two 28 ft bays of perimeter wall on each side).

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

**Selected: intermediate precast shear walls, bearing wall system (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 = ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 row A.5): R = 4, Omega0 = 2.5 (2.0 for collectors - footnote b, flexible diaphragm, SDC-02 s.4), Cd = 4.** The row permits the system in SDC D up to hn = 40 ft (footnote i); Building B has hn = 28 ft (A-101 note 2). Detailing to ACI 318-19 s.18.5 (18.2.1.6 reference).

Why it is the cost-efficient choice (PROC-114 rates, 79 erected panels):

* Ordinary precast shear walls are NP in SDC D (Table 3-1 row A.7) - not permitted.
* Special RC (special precast) walls (row A.1, R = 5, Cd = 5) carry a detailing premium of USD 4,120/panel = USD 325,480 for 79 panels, against USD 1,850/panel = USD 146,150 for intermediate walls; the premium difference (USD 179,330) alone exceeds every saving the 20 % force reduction can buy (the whole deck, connector and tie-down scope of the intermediate design is USD 152,405) and the special option exceeds the USD 395,000 cap. Any joint connector in a special wall would also have to be the JC3 RPC-60D (RPC-CAT-2026 s.2).
* Within intermediate walls the panels are detailed as isolated panel piers (JC0, no vertical joint connectors). Under the DAP-2 Stage A model the coupling force adds to the tie-down of the panels it is delivered to and stiffens the segment (VP-1: k_seg 1,279 vs 769 kip/in, interior-panel tie-down 1.32 vs 0.875 kip per kip), so connectors would cost money and increase tie-down demand. Each panel resists its share of the segment force as a 28 ft cantilever; tie-downs carry the base couple on a 0.8 L lever arm (DAP-2 s.3).

## 3. As-built geometry

The scan CDDC-SV-2026-041 was registered to the building grid on the four high-intensity spheres (rigid transform, rotation -1.742 deg, residuals < 0.0003 ft); the inside faces of the panels fall at X = 0 / 240 and Y = 0 / 180 and the roof openings at RO-1 96-156 x 108-148 and RO-2 36-116 x 36-56. The erected geometry governs (RFI-041, PR-07). Conflicts found and the reading taken:

| Panel layout / count | PCS-014: 81 cast panels | **79 erected panels**: nominal 10 ft panels from each segment start with the closer at the segment end; N-28 and W-15 do not fit the erected wall lines | scan joints (all 46 visible joints lie on this module), PC-101 note 1 |

Wall segments used in Stage A (louver portions are spandrel segments with EI and GAv x 18/28):

## 6. Wall anchorage and the parapet cantilever

* Wp = 1,716 plf per foot of wall (tributary to the roof with the lever action of the parapet). The part delivered by the wall above the top of deck is 100 psf x 3 ft x 29.5/28 = 316.1 plf per foot (parapet transfer).
* Lf per UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 = span of the diaphragm between the walls that support it: 240 ft for the S and N walls, 180 ft for the W and E walls; ka = 1 + Lf/100 capped at 2.0 for all four walls (ASCE 7-22 s.12.11.2.1).
* Fp = 0.4 SDS ka Ie Wp = 755 plf, but not less than 0.2 ka Ie Wp = **858 plf (governs)**.
* Anchors WA2 (embed plate + strap to subdiaphragm tie) at 10 ft on all walls: demand 8.58 k, x 1.4 for steel elements (s.12.11.2.2.2) = 12.01 k <= phi Tn = 0.75 x 18.6 = 13.95 k.
* Continuous cross ties: N-S joist-girder lines at 40 ft for the S/N walls (subdiaphragm 40 ft span x 30 ft deep, L/D 1.33); E-W joist lines on the column lines at 30 ft for the W/E walls (30 ft span x 40 ft deep, L/D 0.75) - both <= 2.5 (s.12.11.2.2.1); the deck is not used as a tie perpendicular to its span (s.12.11.2.2.4). Subdiaphragm shear 572 / 322 plf < phi Sn of the adjacent zones.
* Erection: raking braces 12 kip at 20 ft (ERC-07 s.2, 29 CFR 1926.704(a)); demand 0.5 x 858 plf x 20 ft = 8.6 k; braces removed only after the deck is fastened in that bay.

## 7. Governing constraint per wall line

* **S wall**: governing family = diaphragm_deflection (utilisation 0.97). Other checks: diaphragm_shear 0.94, wall_anchorage 0.86, base_tiedown 0.83, collector_chord 0.61
* **N wall**: governing family = diaphragm_deflection (utilisation 0.97). Other checks: diaphragm_shear 0.91, wall_anchorage 0.86, collector_chord 0.61, base_tiedown 0.50
* **W wall**: governing family = diaphragm_shear (utilisation 0.88). Other checks: wall_anchorage 0.86, base_tiedown 0.75, diaphragm_deflection 0.39, collector_chord 0.36
* **E wall**: governing family = diaphragm_shear (utilisation 0.94). Other checks: wall_anchorage 0.86, base_tiedown 0.65, diaphragm_deflection 0.39, collector_chord 0.26

Tie-downs (BA2, phi Tn = 66 k) per wall: S max 0.83, N max 0.50, W max 0.75, E max 0.65.

## 8. Cost

| item | quantity basis (PROC-114) | USD |
|---|---|---|
| Deck attachment | net zone areas x pattern rate | 80,515 |
| Chords / collectors / drag struts | 20 lines, 2,080 ft of C1 | 23,712 |
| Panel joint connectors | JC0 isolated panel piers | 0 |
| Base tie-downs | 79 erected panels x BA2 | 71,890 |
| Wall anchors | 840 ft / 10 ft = 84 x WA2 | 14,448 |
| SFRS detailing premium | 79 panels x intermediate precast | 146,150 |
| **Total installed cost** | | **336,715** |

Capital cap USD 395,000 (PROC-114 Rev 2, OBD s.5.6): the design is USD 58,285 under the cap (85.2 % of cap).

## 9. Alternatives rejected

* Special precast (special RC) shear walls - premium USD 325,480; even with every other item at its cheapest catalogue option (deck P1 USD 33,712, 20 lines C1 USD 23,712, BA1 USD 41,080, WA1 @ 10 ft USD 8,064) the total would be at least USD 432,048, over the USD 395,000 cap; the R = 5 force reduction cannot offset it.
* Intermediate precast as a building frame system (Table 3-1 B.9, R = 5, Cd = 4.5) - not applicable: the panels are bearing walls carrying the joists (SDC-02 s.4 "bearing-wall shear walls").
* ASCE 7-22 s.12.10.3 (Rs) and s.12.10.4 (RWFD) diaphragm design - excluded by SDC-02 s.5; footnote b would also be void under 12.10.4.
* Ordinary precast shear walls - not permitted in SDC D (Table 3-1 row A.7).
* Joint connectors JC1/JC2 (1-4 per joint, 58 joints) - USD 22,330 to 141,520 extra and, under DAP-2, higher tie-down demand and stiffer segments.
* Uniform deck patterns: uniform P3 fails the zone shears at Z1, Z4, Z8, Z9, Z12 and the construction-stage deflection; uniform P5 costs USD 96,824. Zoned P2-P5 chosen by optimisation (USD 80,515).
* BA1 tie-downs - fail on S, W and E (utilisation up to 1.66) and leave no margin on N; BA3 unnecessary.
* WA1 anchors at 8 ft (USD 10,080) - 6.86 k demand, fails once the 1.4 factor for steel anchorage elements is applied; WA2 at 10 ft adopted.
* Larger chord members (C2-C4) - not required (C1 utilisation <= 0.61).
* ASD format - LRFD gives 7 %% more deck capacity per unit demand (0.60/1.0 vs 0.392/0.7) and 5 %% more for connectors and anchors.
* Cheaper deck sized for the final stage only (USD 69,410) - rejected: it fails the 4.0 in deflection limit in the construction stage (fastened deck cantilevering east from the west wall, S12 and its sign/100-30 permutations, 4.1-5.0 in); the adopted zoning keeps every final and construction case <= 3.88 in.

steps.message:
I've written the package to `output/submission.zip`: the five files at the zip root, built from the templates. My design meets every check in my own implementation of the project's analysis protocol (DAP-2), on all 12 listed cases plus 12 extra variations. It costs **$336,715 against the $395,000 cap**. There's no verifier here, so all of this rests on my own checks.

**Design (LRFD)**
- **Wall system:** intermediate precast shear walls, R = 4, Ω0 = 2.0, Cd = 4, permitted in SDC D up to 40 ft (roof is at 28 ft). Ordinary precast is not permitted in SDC D. The special-precast premium alone ($325k) would put the total over the cap.
- **Panel connections:** no joint connectors anywhere (isolated panels). In the protocol's wall model, connectors stiffen the wall and raise the base tie-down forces, so they add cost and demand.
- **Tie-downs and anchors:** BA2 tie-down on every panel (highest utilisation 0.83). WA2 wall anchors at 10 ft, sized for Fp = 858 plf and the 1.4 factor on steel anchorage parts.
- **Deck:** zones Z1/Z3/Z6/Z9 P5, Z7 P2, all others P4. Highest zone shear utilisation is 0.94.
- **Chords and drag struts:** all 20 lines are required by the design criteria, and the lightest member (L4x4x3/8) works everywhere.
- **Deflection:** worst case is 3.88 in against the 4.0 in limit, governed by the erection stage. With the east deck unfastened, the fastened deck cantilevers off the west wall.
- **Erection braces:** 12 kip at 20 ft.

**How I checked it**
- My wall model reproduces the protocol's worked example (VP-1) exactly.
- My roof model matches hand beam theory exactly.
- Results don't change with how wall springs or roof-unit weights are spread over the mesh.

**Conflicts resolved** (detailed in the design basis and the JSON)
- **Seismic basis:** Risk Category III, Site Class D, SDS 0.44 / SD1 0.24, SDC D. The 2019 Parcel 4B report and the Building A summary don't apply.
- **As-built openings:** taken from the scan, the erection log and RFI-041: D-3 is 15 ft 6 in, the pier between D-4 and D-5 is 14 ft 6 in, L-2 is 16 ft and EY-1 is 44 ft.
- **Wall weight to roof:** 1,716 plf, including the parapet lever action.
- **Ω0:** reduced from 2.5 to 2.0 for a flexible diaphragm, as the design criteria allow.

**Judgement calls that could cost points**
- **About $11k of deck is precautionary.** It covers erection-stage cases that aren't in the shown list (opposite eccentricity sign, 100/30). A deck sized only for the final building ($69.4k) passes the shown erection case S12 only if no roof units are counted or the torsion amplification is taken as large; without that, S12 itself is marginal (4.1 in).
- **Panel count is 79, not the 81 cast.** All 46 joints visible in the scan fit 10 ft panels measured from each segment start. If the checker counts 81, its cost is about $5.5k higher than mine.
- **Wide single panels would break the design.** If the checker reads the scan's missing joints as one-piece wide panels, S and E tie-downs and zone Z8 fail. I rejected that reading because it implies a 72 ft panel on the north wall.
- **Chord capacity is my assumption.** The documents give none; I used 0.9·Fy·Ag. A compression-based capacity could make the lightest member inadequate.
- **Reporting interpretations:**
  - **Wall forces:** they include the parallel walls' own inertia.
  - **S12 torsion factor:** reported as 2.78, which treats the unattached east wall as zero displacement. The design also passes with 1.0.
  - **Governing check per wall:** deflection for S and N, deck shear for W and E. That label is my own definition.

I left 3–6% margin on the critical checks rather than spending more. Each further step costs about $1.2–2k of deck for 1–2% more deflection margin.
